test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 1 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following events related to India's freedom struggle is matched correctly with its year of occurence?

options.text: 1932 - Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, organized the Dalits into the Depressed Classes Association
1922 - Mahatma Gandhi halted the Non-cooperation Movement on the national level as a direct result of the Chauri Chaura incident
1918 - General Dyer opened fire at a gathering at Jallianwala Bagh
1928 - The Indian National Congress passed the resolution on Purna Swaraj

solution:
The correct answer is __**1922 - Mahatma Gandhi halted the Non-cooperation Movement on the national level as a direct result of the Chauri Chaura incident**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **1922 - Mahatma Gandhi halted the Non-cooperation Movement on the national level as a direct result of the Chauri Chaura incident** is correctly matched with its year of occurrence.
 
• The Non-cooperation Movement was a significant phase of the Indian independence movement from British rule, led by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• The movement aimed to resist British rule in India through non-violent means or "Ahimsa".
 
• The Chauri Chaura incident occurred on 4th February 1922, where a violent clash between the police and protesters led to the death of three civilians and 22 policemen.
 
• In response to this violence, Mahatma Gandhi decided to halt the Non-cooperation Movement, emphasizing his commitment to non-violence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar organized the Dalits into the **Depressed Classes Association in 1930**, not 1932.
 
• General Dyer opened fire at a gathering at **Jallianwala Bagh in 1919**, not 1918.
 
• The Indian National Congress passed the resolution on **Purna Swaraj in 1929**, not 1928.
 
• The Non-cooperation Movement was one of the first organized movements of mass civil disobedience (satyagraha) against the British empire.
 
• The movement's suspension was a strategic decision by Gandhi to prevent further escalation of violence and maintain the integrity of the non-violent struggle.
